hints: Notice each row pairs an oscillation direction with an example: parallel means longitudinal and perpendicular means transverse.
Recall that gamma-rays, ultraviolet waves and X-rays are all electromagnetic waves with fields oscillating perpendicular to energy transfer.
Recall that sound is formed by compressions and rarefactions with particle motion parallel to energy transfer, then keep only the row where description and example agree.
walkthrough: Define the two classes: a longitudinal wave has oscillations parallel to the direction of energy transfer, as in sound, while a transverse wave has oscillations perpendicular to the direction of energy transfer.
Classify the examples: gamma-rays, ultraviolet waves and X-rays are all electromagnetic waves and therefore transverse.
Classify sound waves: in air they are longitudinal, with air molecules oscillating back and forth parallel to the direction the sound energy travels.
Check rows A and B: both state parallel oscillations but give gamma-rays and ultraviolet waves, which are transverse, so the description does not fit the example.
Check row C: it states perpendicular oscillations but gives sound waves, which are longitudinal, so the description does not fit the example.
Row D pairs perpendicular oscillations with X-rays, which is correctly transverse electromagnetic radiation. This is option D

options.A: Gamma-rays are electromagnetic waves and are transverse, so oscillations perpendicular to energy transfer, not parallel.
options.B: Ultraviolet waves are electromagnetic waves and are transverse, so oscillations perpendicular to energy transfer, not parallel.
options.C: Sound waves in air are longitudinal, with oscillations parallel to energy transfer, not perpendicular.
options.D: X-rays are electromagnetic waves and are transverse, so oscillations perpendicular to energy transfer is correct.
